question: The future European restriction on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances risks being weakened by the numerous derogations proposed

According to the draft opinion of the Committee for Socio-Economic Analysis of the European Chemicals Agency, numerous derogations to the future general restriction on perand polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), known as ‘forever pollutants’, are being considered.

The document, dated 6 November 2026, proposes allowing PFAS to be used for prolonged periods in sectors such as the chemical industry, semiconductors, batteries and medical devices, with derogations that would, in some cases, apply for 13.5 years after the entry into force of the restriction.

Those potential derogations are cause for concern, given their impact on the effectiveness of the future ban, especially given the persistence of PFAS and the risks they pose to health and the environment. 1.
How will the Commission ensure that the derogations proposed do not undermine the aim of the general restriction on PFAS or compromise the precautionary principle?
Will it require any derogation to be duly justified by the absence of viable alternatives, to be time-limited and to be subject to strictly controlled conditions?
How will it assess the cumulative impact of the derogations on PFAS emissions and ensure that financial interests do not prevail over the protection of health and the environment?
